p2's dark blue monopoly is extremely dangerous with Boardwalk at three houses. p1's red monopoly is uneven and they recently spent $100 on Marvin, so it does not complete the yellow set. I calculated the exact costs to complete a green monopoly. Unmortgaging Pacific would cost $165 and Pennsylvania would cost $176, totaling roughly $341. That is far beyond my $24 cash. I also realized that even if I acquired Pennsylvania, I still could not build houses on it because Pacific remains mortgaged.

A two-player trade is needed to complete the yellow monopoly, which is difficult. I am weighing what to offer p1 and p2 in exchange for their pieces.

I should not give p2 cash, since they need it to build more houses. They are unlikely to trade away their orange or dark blue properties. Denying them Pennsylvania would not hurt their existing monopolies. My light blue properties with three houses remain my main weapon.

I am weighing whether to mortgage STATES, VENTNOR, or NORTH_CAROLINA now. Their current rent is only $10 to $26 because they are not yet monopolies. Keeping them unmortgaged preserves them as trade chips and emergency collateral for future debt resolution.

I am recalculating my total liquidity. I am summing the mortgage values of my remaining properties to verify whether my emergency capacity is closer to $374 or the previously estimated $599.

I realized that mortgaging States and Ventnor would immediately increase my cash to roughly $224. That would make building fourth houses on my light blue properties legal, since the engine updates the game state after each mortgage action. I am now weighing whether the resulting higher rent income justifies the immediate cash outlay.

p1's total liquidation capacity is roughly $893. They can survive a $300 or $450 light blue rent hit, but only by selling all houses first. That would destroy their red monopoly. If they keep their houses, Illinois and Kentucky rent at $300 and $250, which I can cover with my own liquidity.

p2's liquidity is roughly $1084. Eight orange houses sell for $400, and the dark blue houses sell for $500. Their cash plus these house sales easily cover my light blue rent hits.

Building fourth houses would force p2 to strip houses or go bankrupt. The marginal rent gain is small because I only hit one property per turn. Liquidity would still fall to $524, which remains short of New York and Boardwalk.

Building fourth houses would not change the fatal rent thresholds. New York and Boardwalk remain impossible to survive either way. The rent increase is only worthwhile if I can build before opponents land on light blue. Turn 75 is my post-turn after mortgaging Pacific. I am checking whose turn follows next.

p1 is in jail and may not move this turn. p2 is on Marvin Gardens, which sits far from the light blue properties. They would need to roll around the board to reach them, so they will not land there this orbit. This gives me time to build fourth houses before p2 can threaten my light blue set.

Mortgaging Ventnor for $130 yields $154 total cash. That covers the $150 cost of three fourth houses and leaves $4. Liquidity after building would be $524, which is the same as mortgaging both extra properties but preserves States mortgage capacity. I am now weighing whether that remaining $4 is too risky.

I am mapping the standard Monopoly board to check what spaces I can reach from my current position. I am calculating whether a roll from Chance could land me on Park Place or other properties before Boardwalk.

I mapped the full Monopoly board. From my current position on Chance, a roll of 2 would land me on Park Place at $500. That is barely survivable with my current liquidity of $599, but it would be fatal if I had only the reduced $524 after building fourth houses. A roll of 4 would hit Boardwalk at $1400, which is fatal regardless.

I mapped the remaining spaces from my current position. A roll of 2 lands on Park Place, and a roll of 4 lands on Boardwalk. Both are fatal regardless of whether I build fourth houses. The luxury tax is manageable with only $4 cash left, provided I keep States and North Carolina unmortgaged.

I decided to mortgage VENTNOR_AVENUE first. The engine will then ask me again for the house build, since building is not currently an available action. I briefly considered trading a useless property for cash, but p1 and p2 have only $38 and $34 respectively, so they cannot pay much.

I considered trading my railroads or utilities to p2, but they are all mortgaged and would need cash to unmortgage them. That would not help them much given their existing monopolies. I also rejected trading North Carolina or Pacific for Pennsylvania, since p2 already owns that property.

I rejected trading North Carolina to p1 because they only have $38, which is far below the $126 needed for the house build. Losing North Carolina would also destroy my $150 emergency mortgage capacity. I will not give away any yellow properties to either opponent, since that would complete their sets.

Mortgaging North Carolina would leave $24 cash after building fourth houses, compared to only $4 from mortgaging Ventnor. It also preserves the larger $150 mortgage capacity. I am now weighing whether to mortgage North Carolina instead.

Both mortgage options leave total liquidity at $524. Mortgage North Carolina instead of Ventnor would give me a $24 cash cushion rather than $4, which is safer for small charges without needing another action. The rent difference between the two properties is minor.

I will mortgage North Carolina instead of Ventnor. The $24 cash cushion is safer than the $4 left from mortgaging Ventnor, since any charge above $5 would force another mortgage action. Both properties still allow the house build, but North Carolina is the better trade chip.

I will mortgage NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE for $150, leaving $174 in cash. This covers the three fourth houses and leaves $24 remaining. States and Ventnor stay unmortgaged as yellow blockers and emergency mortgages.

I checked whether building fourth houses is actually possible. The bank has five houses left, and the even-build rule allows placing one house on each property. p2 cannot reach my light blue set immediately, so there is no urgency to skip the build.

This differs from an earlier private thought that skipped fourth houses to preserve liquidity for Illinois and Park Place when cash was only $99.

The cash shortfall against New York makes liquidity preservation less important. The goal is now to bankrupt opponents with higher rent before they land on Boardwalk. I will keep my public message brief and avoid revealing the mortgage or house build. I also considered proposing a trade to p2 to defuse Boardwalk, but trades cannot buy immunity.
